events.title: Execution of Joan of Arc
events.description: Joan of Arc, the French military leader who had helped turn the tide of the Hundred Years' War, was burned at the stake in Rouen after being convicted of heresy by an English-backed ecclesiastical court.
events.significance: Joan became a symbol of French national unity and resistance. She was declared innocent in a retrial in 1456, beatified in 1909, and canonized as a saint in 1920.

events.title: Death of Voltaire
events.description: The French Enlightenment writer, historian, and philosopher Voltaire died in Paris at the age of 83, shortly after returning to the city to see the staging of his final play, Irène.
events.significance: Voltaire's advocacy for freedom of speech, religious tolerance, and separation of church and state profoundly influenced the French Revolution and modern liberal thought.

events.title: First Indianapolis 500 Held
events.description: The inaugural Indianapolis 500 auto race was run at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, won by driver Ray Harroun in the Marmon Wasp.
events.significance: The race grew into one of the world's most prestigious motorsport events, and Harroun's use of a rearview mirror is often cited as an early example of the device in racing.

events.title: Dedication of the Lincoln Memorial
events.description: The Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C. was dedicated in a ceremony attended by thousands, including Lincoln's son Robert Todd Lincoln and President Warren G. Harding.
events.significance: The memorial became a national symbol of unity and a major site for civil rights gatherings, most notably Martin Luther King Jr.'s 1963 'I Have a Dream' speech.
